locator: I.13 [30]: That which comes to be anew must take its origin from some innovating cause
interpretation: The finite-past horn: if the world and motion have a first beginning, some cause must be posited for that origin, because what comes to be anew takes its origin from an innovating cause, nothing bringing itself from potency to act or from non-being to being. 'Comes to be anew' is read as either not being at one time and being at a later one, or being at a time before which there is none; 'innovating cause' as a cause other than the thing. What that cause is is not part of the reading.
